Hi Alicia / Sam —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a recommended Dedicated configuration versus Hosted/API option:

- Current ask: real-time summarization + entity extraction for live support chat (low-latency) plus batch nightly enrichment for analytics.
- Key unknowns we need to size Dedicated correctly: sustained TPS (avg and burst), average tokens per request, desired P95 latency SLO for the real-time path, and whether data residency requires VPC/Private deployment.

Can you confirm the following two items so we can produce a short sizing proposal (GPU type + pool size + expected concurrency):
1) Typical request profile — average prompt length and average completion length (tokens), and 95th percentile token length if available.
2) Traffic shape — sustained concurrent requests during business hours, expected bursts (TPS for ~5–10 minutes), and any regional split (US/EU).

For reference, we usually recommend Dedicated when there is a sustained high-throughput path (>500 TPS sustained or consistent multi‑node concurrency) or strict isolation/VPC requirements. For bursty workloads under that, Hosted API with rate-based bursts can still be the lowest-cost path.

If you prefer, we can run a quick capacity worksheet exercise — please attach a short sample of your request token distribution (CSV is fine) and we’ll return a one-page recommendation and rough OPEX estimate by 48 hours.

I’ve attached the NDA and a simple sample_prompts.txt that shows typical prompt shapes we ask for.

Next steps: if you can send the token/profile CSV and confirm whether you need a VPC, I’ll loop in engineering for a sizing run and share a recommended GPU pool (A100/H100/L4 options) + concurrency guidance.

Thanks —

All — looked through the CSV and ran a quick back‑of‑the‑envelope. My recommendations (short):

1) Deployment mode: Hybrid/Dedicated mix — Dedicated pool for real-time chat (VPC peering for prod), Hosted for batch and for overflow bursts beyond pool capacity. This meets VPC requirement and keeps cost reasonable.

2) GPU family & pool sizing (recommended start):
   - Primary: A100 80GB (dense float/quant inference) — good for mixed-length token profiles and stable latency.
   - Pool: 6 A100s to start. Assumptions: ~50 concurrent generator threads per GPU for short-sequence workloads (300 tokens avg) with Redwood runtime batching; sustained ~400–450 TPS covered by 6 GPUs with some headroom for 2–5 minute bursts.
   - Burst handling: configure autoscale/burst to spin up 2 additional nodes (hot spare) on short notice; overflow to Hosted API for extreme spikes (1,200 TPS).

3) Concurrency & TPS rationale:
   - Avg tokens/request ~300 -> ~300 tokens * 400 TPS = 120k tokens/sec sustained. With typical A100 throughput assumptions (model-dependent), 6 GPUs gives reasonable latency headroom.
   - For 95th pct long requests (1,200 tokens), concurrency drops; we recommend a per-route token cap or a fallback lower-capacity model for long-form generation to preserve P95.

4) Batch jobs: run on Hosted reserved scheduled windows or on lower-priority Dedicated nodes (spot-like) overnight. These jobs are token-heavy but low latency — better to use cheaper instance types or time-slice dedicated GPUs.

5) Next ops items:
   - Karthik: can you confirm kernel/quantization profile we'd land on for their preferred model (they liked the open-llm-chat-v2 variant) and whether H100 would materially reduce node count?
   - Tessa: propose a 30-minute sizing workshop with their infra and procurement to walk numbers and confirm peering/network.

Quick cost note (very rough): starting pool (6x A100 80GB, managed + networking + support) ~ $55k–$75k/month depending on commit & data egress assumptions. Hosted overflow usage billed per-token.

I can draft a one-page recommendation for procurement once Karthik confirms quantization/throughput assumptions.

—Ben
